title: Daily Briefing Composer
description: Each school morning the agent speaks a short briefing: today's events, the next test within the window, and the work due soon, then a mascot line. Most of the calendar is left out on purpose: sports and academic events are mentioned only on their own day, and nothing outside the upcoming_days window is read.

learningObjectives: The learner will apply the daily briefing rules to 8 Cedar Ridge events on the morning of Monday, October 19, 2026, by sorting each into the part of the briefing it appears in or "Not mentioned," with at least 7 of the 8 correct.
prerequisites: daily briefing, event category, today's events, next test, due soon, upcoming_days, max_items (all defined in the section "The Daily Briefing and Reminders" above this block).

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

userInterface.layoutPattern: drawing region above a control region

controls.name: Start the 8 events / Back to explore
controls.purpose: Switch between exploring and the quiz.

controls.name: Place menu and Submit
controls.purpose: Choose Today, Next test, Due soon or Not mentioned. One attempt per event.

controls.name: Briefing date, max_items, upcoming_days
controls.purpose: Explore only: any day of the 2026-2027 school year; 1 to 5 items; 1 to 14 days.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Does the briefing list every upcoming event?
Where does a test on the same day go?
Why is a test tomorrow mentioned when a football game in 4 days is not?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The briefing lists every upcoming event. (2) A test on the same day goes under "Next test." (3) A due date 10 days away is "due soon." (4) A test tomorrow is not mentioned because it is not today.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all eight events. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
